summary: Garden seeds and inbox captures have no read path: inspect/related reject every id form tried, search never returns them, and no bootstrap collection lists them, although bootstrap --brief counts them (inbox_items 7, garden_entries 9).
expected: system/OPERATOR.md 'Start here': 'Interfaces must not reconstruct application state by parsing canonical Markdown or YAML. Use list-*, inspect, search, and related for targeted reads.' CLAUDE.md §2: 'for a named record use inspect, search, related, or note-read directly'. The Garden and the inbox are part of the learner's material (OPERATOR.md 'Capture routing'; CLAUDE.md §14 Garden & Harvest).
actual: 'los: record not found' (exit 2) for inspect garden:everything-is-a-dag.md, inspect everything-is-a-dag, related garden:everything-is-a-dag.md, inspect inbox:20260910-tessera-todo.md and inspect 20260910-tessera-todo. search dag returns only concept and note types; search tessera never returns the inbox todo. Connection discovery over these 16 items was possible only by reading knowledge/garden/*.md and work/inbox/*.md directly.
reproduction: python tools/los.py inspect garden:everything-is-a-dag.md   # record not found
python tools/los.py inspect everything-is-a-dag   # record not found
python tools/los.py search dag --limit 30   # result types: concept, note
own_error_possible: An id form or command I did not try might resolve these items (for example a path-shaped id, or a view that exists only in the Obsidian UI). Per protocol I did not read implementation code to find out. The garden.shelve AI action targets 'garden-note' kinds, so the items have ids somewhere, but no documented read reveals them.

summary: related is not symmetric for workspace membership: related WORKSPACE lists the notes the workspace references, but related NOTE does not list that workspace (unless the note itself declares contexts).
expected: CLAUDE.md §2 names related as a lookup for 'a named record', and OPERATOR.md says 'Use list-*, inspect, search, and related for targeted reads.' A relation visible from one end would normally be visible from the other.
actual: related workspace-statlearn-retake includes note-naive-bayes-spam-filter; related note-naive-bayes-spam-filter returns only concept-naive-bayes, source-murphy-pml1 and source-tuh-statlearn-slides. By contrast, related note-oral-exam-prep-strategy includes workspace-os-oral-prep, because that note declares the workspace in its own contexts.
own_error_possible: related may be defined as 'the record's own outgoing references' by design; no document I read states its direction, so this may be intended behaviour rather than a defect.

summary: The documented cross-domain discovery entry, generated/domain-atlas.md, does not exist in the freshly built world; generated/ holds only derived-state/.
expected: CLAUDE.md §2: 'For cross-domain discovery, consult the At a glance block of the current generated/domain-atlas.md before narrowing.' CLAUDE.md 'Cross-domain reach (ADR-005)': 'open the full generated/domain-atlas.md and check the shelves of ALL domains'. system/WORKFLOWS.md lists domain-atlas.md among the generated views.
actual: ls generated/ shows only derived-state, before and after all S03 reads. The bootstrap --brief domain_atlas glance reports 0 shelves, 0 crosswalks and 0 entries in every domain, so a generated atlas would add only note counts here. I did not run los generate: it writes derived files, and S27 asked for no changes.
own_error_possible: The atlas is presumably produced by los generate. EVAL-WORLD.json records generate_exit 0 for the build, yet the file is absent at first contact, so this may come from the eval world builder rather than the product; hence AMBIGUOUS.
